chapter_note: The chapter opens with a dialogue-attribution frame and then preserves a short core sequence describing Matter’s envy across key cosmological/primordial moments (First Man; image of the Ambassador; Adam). From ¶5 onward the language shifts into Christian overlay (Christ/cross/apostles) and then into explicitly Mani-and-church material with strong pastoral drift (catechumens, exhortation), matching the chapter-level fatigue signal. ¶7–9 are admonitory/paraenetic expansions rather than systematic cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] entirety of envy is this first nature that occu[red] in the worlds of darkness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue-attribution frame: "Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:" (hagiographic compilation voice; 'apostle' marker).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening attribution to the apostle + disciples is a compilation frame, but the remaining sentence is impersonal cosmological definition (envy as a primordial nature in the worlds of Darkness).

paragraphs.core_text: In this envy that [ ... ] in it, the First Man [ ... ] its poiso[n ... ] its evil-doing. His garment[s] were [ ... ] it cut them and drew them; [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic mythic-cosmological register (First Man; hostile action of Darkness/Matter; garment imagery) with no citation, exhortation, or institutional vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.179⟩ It envied the first image of the Ambassador, which he displayed to it in the heights abov[e], i[n] his form that it saw. It established the seal and the image of flesh, and put the impression of t[h]at image on flesh, its very own birth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmogonic mechanism: Ambassador as named cosmic being; image/seal/impression on flesh described as process (impersonal explanatory voice).

paragraphs.core_text: [The th]ird time it envied Adam, the fir[st hum]an. It seized a power from him, and bore it forth from a [rib of] of Adam's [flesh].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Primordial-anthropogonic episode stated as a numbered sequence (“third time”); no church address or NT citation formula; fits the older teaching’s mythic causality.

Christian overlay: explicit “blessed Christ,” “father of all the apostles,” and “wood of the cross” are NT-derived/Christianized narrative identifiers rather than the impersonal cosmological exposition of the core.

Mani self-reference (“I myself was sent… last generation”), plus explicit institutional vocabulary (church, assembly, catechumens) and direct exhortation to listeners; this matches the strong second-half pastoral drift.

Paraenetic description of how envy attacks ‘inside’ and ‘outside’ via sickness and slander, aimed at community figures (“teacher,” “righteous elect person”); admonitory/community-protective register rather than systematic cosmology.

Community-directed warning about the ‘lesser in power’ falling from faith, and the extension “until my time… to my church” ties the passage to Mani/community situation; not a closed cosmological mapping.
General moral exhortation (“appropriate for the wise person… steadfast… faith/hope”) without cosmological mechanism; classic late admonition/closing material.
